_meta.description: Mapping table: an Uberhand/4IFIR Wizard settings backup -> the CUST offsets of our field map. USED BY scripts/make-factory-defaults.mjs to turn the firmware's own Default.json into package/factory-defaults.json, which the generator then turns into service/Default.ini. It is also the groundwork for importing users' old backups - see docs/CONVERTER-CONCEPT.md; that import is deferred and NO menu section is generated from this file today.
_meta.source_format: atmosphere/kips/kip-json/*.json — an array of 54 entries, each with a parameter name, a hex value and the internal fields extent/filler_before/page. The entry order is stable, verified on Default.json and Eclipse.json.
_meta.why_explicit: The mapping is spelled out EXPLICITLY rather than matched by name. Automatic matching sends the voltage curve points to the wrong places: the point names of the Mariko and Erista curves are identical ("307MHz"), so a name match picks an arbitrary one. The converter writes into a live kip, and a miss here corrupts a table nobody will ever find afterwards.
_meta.platform: There is NO need to work out the revision from the file: the converter runs on the console, and the engine filters out the other revision's fields by the ;system= tag. Fields with platform mariko/erista are applied only on their own revision.
_meta.length: Where the backup has 4 bytes and the map has 3 — the top byte is always zero, the value is little-endian, and the first three bytes are taken. Verified against both reference files.

singles.note: CPUv. Both stages and millivolts — carried over as is
marikoCpuMaxVolt. On Erista the maximum lives at 20 — the engine filters by ;system=
marikoGpuUV. WARNING: value 03 switches the voltage table on. Carried over as is — the state has to match the source
marikoEmcMaxClock. On Erista the frequency is at 24 — the Uberhand backup has no separate entry for it
eBAMATIC Stage = pMEH[18]. The backup name has two leading spaces — that is how the original spells it

series.note: THE RUN IS NOT CONTIGUOUS. drochr01..07 sit back to back at 60…84, but the eighth (drochr08) lives apart at 12356. A "start plus stride" calculation would land on 88 — the first point of the Mariko curve.
Element 18 of the array (offset 12436) is the same eBAMATIC Stage as entry 14. The values must agree; if they disagree, trust this entry — it comes from the pMEH array itself.

skipped.why: A separator heading, carries no value

The values are stored in MICROvolts (307 MHz → 485000) while marikoGpuVoltArray holds millivolts (factory 395, 420, 445…). The numbers match neither in scale nor in value — this is not the same field. Until we work out where Uberhand got them from, the curve is not imported at all: the existing one is left untouched.
